summary: SHIP VERDICT: DO-NOT-SHIP, on two blockers, and the first one is not a defect in this item's code. (1) Removing the four publish.py EXCLUDE lines ships a FILE, not a CAPABILITY. `/veldo:init` lays down 43 files and NONE of the estimation layer: not cost_to_change.py, not toe_corpus.py, not metrics.py, not spend.py. Measured on a fixture carrying exactly what init lays down plus the module hand-installed, `python3 .veldo/cost_to_change.py` exits 1 with `FileNotFoundError: .veldo/toe_corpus.py`. That is ledger finding 61's exact shape and its exact measurement method, so an adopter receives a fragment. The repair is PLAN-0014 W10's footprint, not this item's, which is why the honest answer is: land the fixes below and ship this WITH W10, not before it. (2) The map contradicts itself in the data on FIRST REAL USE, with the exact command the remediation itself used: `python3 .veldo/spend.py record --spec WARP-0100 --basis harness_reported --tokens 750000` yields `usable_as_cost_ground_truth: true` with cost_notice ABSENT and every one of the ten areas reading `tokens=None ... (unrecorded, spend on 0 of N)`, and the 750000 tokens appear in no figure anywhere, because WARP-0100 is UNATTRIBUTED and that bucket carries only records, specs and reason. AC4's live RECORDED arm passed over that state because its per-area legs iterate `_w1409_live_areas_of.get(_s, ())`, empty for an unattributed spec, so every all(...) in it is vacuously true. A blunt boolean claiming cost ground truth over a map with no cost in it is precisely the number this item exists to stop a reader quoting. TEETH: all 8 criteria's declared falsifications were driven in an isolated copy, 12 mutations, each diffed to prove it landed, and every one reddened the row its own field names, with each named control staying green; 4 of the 12 are additive. Line numbers in every falsified_by field are accurate, which after ledger 34 is worth saying. THE LANDMINE CLASS IS GENUINELY CLOSED: recording spend leaves the WHOLE suite set at 4723 passed, 0 failed, unchanged from baseline. Every published figure reproduces exactly (174 records, 90 memberships, 66 attributed, 108 unattributed, 66 placement, 0 git path, cost_coverage 0.0) and the load-bearing structural claim is exact: 0 of 1003 gate events carry a spec_id or correlation_id. FOUR MAJORS beyond the declarations: the two stand-downs are routed through shared.no_history with a PROSE SENTENCE where the mechanism wants a module path, so `history_begins_with` (the guard that separates an absent input from a BROKEN READER) answers True in every repository forever, and gutting the ONE git reader in both twins leaves the suite at 40 passed 0 failed; AC8's headline count-equals-the-read is 0 == 0 today and hardcoding files_touched to zeros is green, while `toe_corpus._run` already takes the `cwd` that ledger 60's prescribed fixture seam needs; AC6's clause `nothing reads a clock, mints an id or writes a file` is defended by nothing, proven by making report() write a file into .veldo and watching 40 passed 0 failed; and `repo_report(root=X)` honours X for the contract and the specs while reading the event stream, the git history and the protected patterns from wherever the module lives.

criteria.note: Drove the declared falsification (deleted the `if declared:` early return at .veldo/cost_to_change.py:267-269 in both twins), diffed it, and the named row went red: suite:210 declaration-wins, together with the named live-map leg at suite:990 reading WARP-1401 back as basis placement in the metrics area (32 passed, 9 failed from a clean 40/0). The claims were then checked in the code rather than in the prose: `arch.footprint_areas` filters placement to `area_ids(contract)`, so an unresolving placement really does resolve to nothing (suite drives that with placement [nowhere_at_all]); and `.veldo/entropy.py` resolves through the SAME `arch.footprint_areas` / `arch.area_for_path`, so `the two maps can never disagree about where a change landed` holds rather than being asserted. Front matter does arrive through validate.parse_yamlish, injected. One imprecision reported as F8 rather than as a refutation: the front-matter BLOCK slicer here is a third regex, different from toe_corpus._front_matter and validate.front_matter, and a spec the corpus accepts but this slicer drops is silently reported as declaring no placement.

Drove the declared falsification (stamped BY_PLACEMENT in the stand-down return at :275-276 in both twins) and the named in-the-data row at suite:251-258 went red on the per-area attribution count, the member basis_label, git_path_attributed, the bases entry and the notice, all read after json.dumps (35 passed, 5 failed). The placement-only negative control at suite:270-274 STAYED GREEN, which is what proves the mislabel was removed and not the warning. The AC's central property, that the weaker join says so in the data a consumer reads, is real and defended. TWO GAPS, both reported as findings. F2: the LIVE half of this join stands down by name, and its stand-down condition cannot fail, so the real reader is defended by nothing at all in this repository or any other; gutting `git_touched` in both twins leaves the suite at 40 passed 0 failed. F7: `basis` is recorded per RECORD but consumed per (record, area), and 14 of the 66 live placement-basis records reach at least one of their areas ONLY through footprint globs, so those area lines carry a label reading `PLAN-0011 W3 declaration present` for an area the placement never named.

Drove the declared falsification (replaced the unattributed branch of report at :404-406 with a default into the first declared contract area) and all three named rows went red: the partition set equality at suite:315-318 (unattributed.specs emptied while WARP-9404 appeared inside an area), the memberships identity at suite:326-330, and the live-map leg at suite:992 requiring WARP-0100 to be unattributed (32 passed, 8 failed). The partition really is one enumeration compared as set equality and disjointness rather than two counts, over the fixture AND over the live repository against an independently built corpus. The cross-area rule (each area gets the whole cost, nothing divided) is asserted with WARP-9403 crossing two areas and area_memberships 4 over 4 records. Nothing to add.

Both declared legs have teeth: deleting the unrecorded guard in `_sum_cost` at :345-347 reds suite:433-439, the live derived per-area equality at suite:1088 and the cost stand-down arm at suite:1167-1171 while the recorded-spend positive control at suite:453-460 stays green (36 passed, 4 failed); deleting the `if count else None` at :323 reds suite:395-408 and the live gate stand-down arm at suite:1205-1209 (36 passed, 4 failed). The landmine remediation is real and I verified it the way ledger 26 prescribes: one sanctioned `python3 .veldo/spend.py record --spec WARP-0100 --basis harness_reported --tokens 750000` left the WHOLE suite set at 4723 passed, 0 failed, byte-identical to baseline. WHAT REFUTES THE CRITERION is what that same command then makes the map SAY. AC4's own text promises `the basis, the coverage ratio and the notices must agree with those counts`. Measured: usable_as_cost_ground_truth true, cost_notice ABSENT, cost_known_records 1, and all ten areas reading tokens=None with cost_basis unrecorded and spend on 0 of N. The notice is gated on a CORPUS-level boolean while the sentence it carries is an AREA-level statement, so the one explanation of the None disappears exactly when a reader most needs it, and the recorded 750000 tokens are in no figure at all. The live RECORDED arm did not catch it because every per-area leg in it iterates `_w1409_live_areas_of.get(_s, ())`, which is empty for an unattributed spec, so the arm is a check that cannot fail for the state the first use produces. See F1 and F9.

Both declared legs have teeth. Deleting `refuse_malformed(corpus)` at :393 reds exactly the three named rows, the eight-shape refusal at suite:509-518, the named-spec refusal at suite:523-525 and the duplicate-spec refusal at suite:527-532, while the well-formed positive control at suite:534-539 stays green (37 passed, 3 failed). The one-enumeration leg was driven ADDITIVELY: giving check_corpus a second problem spelling behind :212 reds exactly suite:548-558 and nothing else (39 passed, 1 failed), because that row compares the two surfaces as SETS OF MESSAGES rather than as two counts. The eight-shape table is bound to its own length, and each expected fragment names the field. This is the strongest criterion in the item.

The two DECLARED legs are confirmed with teeth. Deleting the empty-corpus stand-down at :390-392 reds suite:565-585 including the coverage-block key equality at suite:584 (38 passed, 2 failed). The outside-the-gate leg was driven ADDITIVELY as the field prescribes: making `scripts/secret_inventory.py`, a required stage, LOAD the module reds exactly suite:868 (39 passed, 1 failed), and the derived domain is genuinely derived, since the same run proves the stage set covers the six required scripts plus validate.py, shape_gate.py and events.py and the closure is strictly larger. WHAT IS NOT EVIDENCED is the rest of the criterion's own sentence: `nothing reads a clock, mints an id or writes a file`. I added one line to report() writing `.veldo/ctc_side_effect.json`, proved the file existed on disk afterwards, and the suite stayed at 40 passed, 0 failed. Determinism across two in-process runs and a reversed corpus cannot see a write, and the spawn scanner looks for subprocess primitives, not for filesystem writes. The property holds in today's code, which I read; nothing defends it. Ledger 53's prescription (a recursive inventory of path, size, mtime and sha256 before and after) is the known fix. See F4.

Both legs driven ADDITIVELY and both red the named row. Adding a fifth loader call for `.veldo/entropy.py` beside the four in repo_report reds the dependency-surface row at suite:750-751, because _W1409_LOADS is harvested from the module's own source at suite:742 and then carries a fifth path (37 passed, 3 failed, the two extra being the wiring rows whose stub loader KeyErrors on the new path and correctly turns that into a red rather than a crash). Importing subprocess reds the no-spawn row at suite:777 (39 passed, 1 failed), and that scanner carries its own positive control over a planted text. The allow-listed metrics to contracts edge is read out of the real `.veldo/architecture.yaml` rather than the fixture. I confirmed independently that `.veldo/entropy.py` names cost_to_change nowhere and resolves areas through the same two arch functions, so C6's seam really is prose plus a shared resolver.

The declared falsification has teeth for the KEY SET only: renaming the count key at .veldo/toe_corpus.py:176 reds suite:887-890 and the absent-spec control at suite:900-901 (38 passed, 2 failed). The criterion's HEADLINE property, `files_touched COUNTS exactly what git_touched READS`, is evidenced by nothing. Driven: hardcoding `files_touched` to `{commits: 0, files_touched: 0}` in both twins, which is a wrong number in every one of the 174 WARP-1401 corpus records the whole plan trains on, left the suite at 40 passed, 0 failed. The count-equals-the-read leg is 0 == 0 here, which the falsified_by field discloses honestly; what is NOT disclosed is that the non-empty control is routed through shared.no_history with a prose sentence as the module path, so the guard meant to separate an absent input from a broken reader cannot fail, and gutting `git_touched` itself is equally green. The fix is not a new mechanism: `toe_corpus._run(args, cwd=None)` already takes the cwd, so a throwaway git repository with one commit naming a fixture spec id would drive both readers non-vacuously EVERYWHERE, with no history dependency and no stand-down. That is ledger 60's own prescription, and it was three lines away. See F2 and F3.

findings.text: SHIPPING THIS BY DELETING THE publish.py EXCLUDE LINES SHIPS A FILE, NOT A CAPABILITY, AND THE ADOPTER GETS A TRACEBACK. `/veldo:init` lays down 43 files and none of PLAN-0014's estimation layer: cost_to_change.py, toe_corpus.py, metrics.py and spend.py are all absent from init_scaffold._FILES and from REQUIRED_SUBSTRATE. So an adopter who installs the pack receives engine/.veldo/cost_to_change.py inside the plugin and their repository never gets it; and if they hand-install it, the module's first call loads four siblings of which two are not there either. This is ledger finding 61 in a new organ, and finding 61's own lesson applies unchanged: an install check that proves the adopter's GATE runs does not prove the product runs, and the adopter's gate never invokes this module (AC6 asserts exactly that, correctly). The repair belongs to PLAN-0014 W10, whose title is `so /veldo:init lays them down and the packs carry them`, so this is not a defect in WARP-1409's code and it is still a reason not to ship WARP-1409 on its own.
findings.evidence: Enumerated init_scaffold._FILES in process: `.veldo/cost_to_change.py laid down by /veldo:init: False`, `.veldo/toe_corpus.py False`, `.veldo/metrics.py False`, `.veldo/spend.py False`, against `.veldo/validate.py True`, `.veldo/arch.py True`, `.veldo/policy_check.py True`. Built a fixture tree holding exactly init's laid-down set plus engine/.veldo/cost_to_change.py, git init'd it, and ran the module: `exit: 1`, `stderr tail: FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/tmp/adopter1409-jobq9_ej/.veldo/toe_corpus.py'`. Also measured: publish.py's INCLUDE is ('engine/**', 'packs/**', 'docs/*.md', 'docs/training/**', README.md, VELDO.md, LICENSE, NOTICE, CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, SECURITY.md, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json), so scripts/suites/15_warp_1409_*.py does NOT ship and none of AC6's gate-domain pins can redden an adopter gate. The module is named in no shipped document and has no `.veldo/capabilities.yaml` entry (0 hits). FIX SHAPE: ship it with W10, which adds it and its siblings to _FILES, or not at all.

findings.text: ON FIRST REAL USE THE REPORT'S HEADLINE BOOLEAN CONTRADICTS EVERY NUMBER UNDER IT, THE NOTICE THAT WOULD EXPLAIN THE CONTRADICTION IS SUPPRESSED BY THE SAME EVENT, AND AC4's OWN LIVE ARM CANNOT FAIL THERE. `cost_known` and therefore `usable_as_cost_ground_truth` and the presence of `cost_notice` are computed over the WHOLE corpus, including records that are UNATTRIBUTED; the per-area cost fields are computed over each area's own members. Record spend against an unattributed spec and the two disagree: the map announces itself usable as cost ground truth while every area reports tokens None with cost_basis unrecorded, and the recorded tokens are reported nowhere at all, because `unattributed` carries only records, specs and reason. The state is reached by ONE command, and it is the very command the remediation used for its own proof, on a spec (WARP-0100) that this suite itself asserts is unattributed. AC4's recorded arm is written as `all(... for _s in _w1409_live_spend_of for _a in _w1409_live_areas_of.get(_s, ()))`, and `.get(_s, ())` is empty for an unattributed spec, so the arm is vacuously true exactly in the state that produces the incoherence. This is the item's own named failure mode: a figure a reader will quote without asking how it was derived, with the disclosure removed rather than carried.
findings.evidence: Baseline `python3 scripts/selftest.py` -> `selftest: 4723 passed, 0 failed`. Then `python3 .veldo/spend.py record --spec WARP-0100 --basis harness_reported --tokens 750000` (accepted, one veldo.event/v1 appended). Suite -> `40 passed`, full set -> `4723 passed, 0 failed` (so the landmine class IS closed). Then `python3 .veldo/cost_to_change.py`: the report prints only the CYCLES notice, no COST line, and each of the ten areas prints `cost: tokens=None cost_usd=None human_minutes=None (unrecorded, spend on 0 of N)`. repo_report() read back: `usable_as_cost_ground_truth: True`, `cost_known_records: 1`, `cost_notice present: False`, `WARP-0100 unattributed: True`, `per-area tokens: {contracts: None, distribution: None, docs: None, enforcement: None, engine: None, fleet: None, loop: None, metrics: None, runners: None, tracker: None}`, `per-area cost_basis: ['unrecorded']`. FIX SHAPE: gate the notice on whether any ATTRIBUTED record carried spend (or emit a second notice naming the recorded-but-unattributed count), give the unattributed bucket its own cost and cycles blocks so nothing recorded is absent from every figure, and make the live recorded arm require that every spend-recording spec is either in an area reporting `recorded` OR counted in a named unattributed-spend figure, so the arm cannot be satisfied by an empty iteration.

findings.text: THE TWO STAND-DOWNS ARE ROUTED THROUGH A GUARD THAT CANNOT FAIL, SO A BROKEN GIT READER STANDS DOWN INSTEAD OF REDDENING, IN EVERY REPOSITORY FOREVER. `shared.no_history(inputs, ...)` takes `(module path, resolved revision or None)` pairs and stands down only when every unresolved input also satisfies `history_begins_with(module_path)`; its docstring is explicit that it returns False `in every other case, including a repository with history whose revision lookup failed - that is a defect and the caller must assert exactly as it always did`, and that `only a leg REQUIRING a pre-change revision may be routed through here`. WARP-1409 passes the strings `the commits naming WARP-1401` and `the commits naming any spec of the live actuals corpus`. `history_begins_with` runs `git log --format=%H --reverse -- <rel>` and returns True when the result is empty, which a non-path always is, so the discrimination is destroyed: the mechanism can no longer tell an honestly absent input from a reader that is broken, and neither leg is about a pre-change revision in the first place. The consequence is not theoretical: gutting `git_touched`, the ONE reader the whole git-path stand-down depends on, in both twins, leaves the suite at 40 passed, 0 failed. The printed reason is also false as a sentence a gate reader can check, since it names a file that does not exist and a revision that was never resolved, which is ledger 69's family of a record whose subject is not what it appears to name.
findings.evidence: Measured in the copy: `history_begins_with('the commits naming WARP-1401') = True    revisions found: 0`, `history_begins_with('the commits naming any spec of the live actuals corpus') = True    revisions found: 0`, against `history_begins_with('.veldo/toe_corpus.py') = True   revisions found: 1` and `('.veldo/cost_to_change.py') = True   revisions found: 2` (this tree is per-file flattened, so a correctly spelled argument happens to agree HERE, and would not in an adopter tree that has accumulated revisions). ATTACK 1, diffed and applied to both twins: `out = ""` / `shas = []` inside git_touched -> `15_warp_1409_cost_to_change_per_area  40 passed  0.16s`, `selftest (PARTIAL): 66 passed, 0 failed` (the 1.14s -> 0.16s drop is the git work disappearing, unobserved by any assertion). FIX SHAPE: pass the real module path to no_history so the guard can answer, and split the leg the way the mechanism demands, by driving both readers over an injected `cwd` fixture repository rather than over this repository's history.

findings.text: AC8's HEADLINE IS DEFENDED ONLY BY THE KEY SET, AND THE FIXTURE SEAM THAT WOULD FIX IT ALREADY EXISTS. `files_touched` can be replaced by hardcoded zeros with the suite fully green, so the count-equals-the-read property, the property the criterion is named for, is unevidenced. The blast radius is not this module: `toe_corpus.build` puts that dict into every one of the 174 WARP-1401 corpus records as the spec's `git` block, which is the mechanical feature the estimator, the analogy layer and the reconciliation records all read. The falsified_by field honestly discloses that both sides read 0 here; what it does not say is that the remedy needed no new mechanism, because `toe_corpus._run(args, cwd=None)` already accepts a working directory and `git_touched` simply does not pass one. Ledger 60 wrote the prescription for exactly this: a property only a differently shaped tree can exhibit needs a SEAM to be asked about that tree, and the seam is part of the fix rather than a convenience.
findings.evidence: ATTACK 2, diffed and applied to both twins: `files_touched` body replaced by `return {"commits": 0, "files_touched": 0}` -> `15_warp_1409_cost_to_change_per_area  40 passed`, `selftest (PARTIAL): 66 passed, 0 failed`. Read in the source: `def _run(args, cwd=None): r = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=str(cwd or ROOT))`, and `git_touched` calls `_run(["git", "log", ...])` with no cwd. FIX SHAPE: `git_touched(spec_id, root=None)` threading root into both `_run` calls, `files_touched(spec_id, root=None)` forwarding it, and one suite row that git init's a throwaway tree, commits a file with a message naming WARP-9401, and requires commits and files non-empty with each count equal to its list's length. That runs everywhere and retires the stand-down.

findings.text: AC6 CLAIMS THE MODULE WRITES NOTHING AND NOTHING CHECKS IT. The criterion's text says `nothing reads a clock, mints an id or writes a file`, and that is a safety claim an adopter relies on for a module the spec calls adoption safe. The suite's coverage is determinism across two in-process runs plus a reversed corpus, and a spawn-primitive scanner. Neither can see a filesystem write, and the write I added is not a contrived one: report() is the entry point a consumer calls, and a future edit that caches or stamps anything would land there. The declared falsification for AC6 names the stand-down and the gate domain and never names this clause, so the criterion asserts more than it defends. The property does hold in today's code, which I read line by line: the only imports are argparse, importlib.util, json, re, sys and pathlib, and there is no open, write_text or mkdir anywhere.
findings.evidence: ATTACK 3, additive, diffed and applied to both twins: one line after `refuse_malformed(corpus)` writing `(Path(ROOT) / '.veldo' / 'ctc_side_effect.json').write_text(json.dumps({'wrote': True}))` -> `selftest (PARTIAL): 66 passed, 0 failed`, and the file was really on disk afterwards: `-rw-rw-r-- 1 dmitry dmitry 15 Aug 13 05:23 .veldo/ctc_side_effect.json`. FIX SHAPE: ledger 53's own repair, a recursive inventory of path, size, mtime and sha256 over the tree under report() before and after the call, asserted identical, with an additive control proving the inventory can see a planted write.

findings.text: `repo_report(root=X)` HONOURS X FOR TWO OF ITS FIVE INPUTS AND SILENTLY READS THE OTHER THREE FROM WHEREVER THE MODULE LIVES. The contract comes from `V.load_repo_contract(repo_root=str(base))` and the specs from `base / 'specs'`, but the EVENT STREAM comes from `M.load()` (metrics.LOG, an absolute path under the module's own ROOT), the GIT HISTORY from `TC.git_touched` (toe_corpus.ROOT), and the PROTECTED PATTERNS from `PC.protected_patterns()`. So a per-area cost map produced for repository X carries repository Y's cycles, spend and git attribution, with nothing in the report saying which tree each figure came from, and the docstring calls this function `the CLI's one wiring point` without mentioning that root is partial. The suite cannot see it, because the wired block substitutes all three of those readers with stubs and the live block passes no root. No user gets a wrong answer from the CLI today, since main() passes no root; the parameter is public, the entropy organ is the intended consumer, and a half honoured root is the shape a caller cannot detect.
findings.evidence: Measured: `toe_corpus.ROOT : <the work copy>`, `metrics LOG path : <the work copy>/.veldo/events.jsonl`. Built another git repository holding ONE shipped spec (WARP-9501, placement metrics) plus a copy of this tree's architecture.yaml, then `repo_report(root=OTHER)` -> `records=1 areas=['metrics']`, with the git reader consulted being the work copy and not the root passed. FIX SHAPE: either thread root through all five reads (metrics.load(root=), toe_corpus.git_touched(root=), policy_check.protected_patterns(root=)) or drop the parameter and let the loader seam carry test wiring, which is what the suite actually uses it for.

findings.text: THE SUITE AND THE SPEC BOTH STATE, AS FACT, THAT NOTHING ELSE GUARDS THE ENGINE TWINS, AND SOMETHING ALREADY DOES. The twin-comparison row asserts in its own text `Nothing else in this repository compares either pair`, and the spec's Out of scope records the gate level enforcement as `a one-line-per-pair change to that script and is recorded here rather than made`. Both describe a `scripts/check_template_sync.sh` that no longer exists: ledger finding 3 replaced its hand written PAIRS map with pairs DERIVED from `git ls-files engine`, and both `engine/.veldo/cost_to_change.py` and `engine/.veldo/toe_corpus.py` are tracked, so both pairs are already compared by a gate stage. The harm is not a wrong number, it is a false statement inside an assertion's own evidence text and a to-do recorded as outstanding when it is done, which is the ledger 19 and 68 family at small size. The redundancy itself is harmless and worth keeping.
findings.evidence: `bash scripts/check_template_sync.sh` -> `template sync: pass (122 pair(s) compared, 6 declared per-repo, 131 engine-only)`. `git ls-files engine | grep cost_to_change` -> `engine/.veldo/cost_to_change.py`. Appended two lines to engine/.veldo/cost_to_change.py only -> `FAIL: .veldo/cost_to_change.py drifted from engine/.veldo/cost_to_change.py` / `template sync: FAIL` / `exit=1`. FIX SHAPE: reword both to say the derived stage guards the pair and this row is a second, cheaper reader of the same fact.

findings.text: THE BASIS IS RECORDED PER RECORD AND CONSUMED PER (RECORD, AREA), SO 14 AREA LINES CLAIM A PLACEMENT DECLARATION FOR AN AREA THE PLACEMENT NEVER NAMED. `arch.footprint_areas` returns the placement's areas UNION the areas the footprint globs fall into, and `attribute` stamps one basis for the record. BASIS_LABELS[placement] then reads `joined on the spec's DECLARED placement (PLAN-0011 W3 declaration present and resolving to contract areas)` beside every area the record joined, including areas that came only from a footprint glob. Measured live: all 66 placement-basis records do declare a resolving placement, so no record is mislabelled, but 14 of them contribute at least one area that the placement does not name. The join is still a human declaration and PLAN-0011's entropy map resolves identically, so the two maps do not disagree and this is not a fabricated join; the label just names the wrong declaration at area granularity, in a module whose entire thesis is that the basis is exact.
findings.evidence: Measured over the live map: `placement-basis specs: 66`, `of those, declaring NO usable placement key: 0`, `specs whose reported areas include areas that came ONLY from footprint globs: 14`, e.g. `('WARP-0614', placement ['tracker'], footprint-only ['docs'])`, `('WARP-0711', ['engine'], ['enforcement'])`, `('WARP-0717', ['engine'], ['docs', 'enforcement'])`. FIX SHAPE: resolve the basis per (record, area) (placement_declared vs footprint_declared vs git_path) or widen the label to `declared placement or footprint`.

findings.text:
A THIRD FRONT-MATTER BLOCK SLICER, AND A SPEC IT DROPS IS REPORTED AS DECLARING NOTHING, COUNTED NOWHERE. AC1's claim of one parser is true of the PARSING and not of the SLICING, which the docstring concedes. `front_matter_index` uses `re.match(r'^---
(.*?)
---', text, re.S)`; `toe_corpus._front_matter` uses `text.startswith('---')` plus `text.find('
---', 3)`; `validate.front_matter` uses `^---
(.*?)
---
`. The corpus and the index are therefore built by two different readers over one directory, and where they disagree, or where parse_yamlish raises, the index `continue`s silently and the record is reported with `basis: git_path` or `unattributed` carrying a label that says the spec declares no resolving placement. That is a claim about the spec, not about the reader, and no `unreadable` or `unparsed` count exists anywhere in the report to qualify it. Ledger 39 is the same defect in floor_report and was fixed there by putting an unreadable list in the report shape. Measured today: zero specs diverge, so this is latent rather than active.
findings.evidence: In the copy: `corpus records: 174  fm index entries: 213`, `CORPUS RECORDS WITH NO FRONT-MATTER INDEX ENTRY: 0`, `SPEC FILES THE INDEX DROPPED: 0` (checking both the regex miss and a parse_yamlish ValueError). Read the three slicers side by side: cost_to_change.py:241, toe_corpus.py:63-66, validate.py:48. FIX SHAPE: take the block from the one reader the corpus already uses, and carry an `unreadable` list plus its count in the report, named in the notice, with a driven row over two specs where one cannot be sliced.

findings.text: THE UNATTRIBUTED BUCKET CARRIES NO COST AND NO CYCLE TOTALS, SO 108 OF 174 RECORDS' RECORDED SIGNALS ARE ABSENT FROM EVERY FIGURE IN THE REPORT. `unattributed` holds exactly records, specs and reason. AC3 is right that nothing may be spread or defaulted into an area, and reporting the unattributed set's OWN totals beside its count is not spreading anything; it is the difference between a record that is counted and a record whose cost is invisible.
